target_customer: Startups and small companies wanting press coverage without a monthly PR agency retainer
problem: Traditional PR agencies charged retainers of $5,000 to $20,000 a month. Upbeat offered software plus a media strategist to turn a company's story into an interactive pitch sent to journalists.
business_model: Software-powered PR agency: $800 first campaign plus annual membership, $500 per later campaign (VentureBeat 2017)

founders.name: Ricky Yean
founders.background_notes: Named by VentureBeat 2017 as CEO; not on the YC page.

founders.name: David Tran
founders.background_notes: YC page calls him founder and CTO and says he wrote the first lines of code for Alchemy.

founders.name: Mark Linsey
founders.background_notes: Listed as a founder on the YC page only.

technical_complexity.rationale: Interactive press pages and outreach tooling are standard web engineering; the media database was the larger build.

defensibility.rationale: The service still relied on human strategists, and PR tools were widely copyable; a media database was planned but not shown to be a moat.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Cision and Vocus merged in 2014 per a search snippet; no source shows them copying Upbeat.

market_need_then: VentureBeat (2017) says Upbeat served over 300 companies and contrasted its $800 campaigns with agency retainers of $5,000 to $20,000.

rebrands.why: VentureBeat 2017 says PRX was renamed Upbeat; reason not given and exact date not stated.

brand_strength.rationale: Covered by VentureBeat, Nieman Lab and PYMNTS at its 2017 funding, but no mascot or community evidence.

pivots.to: PRX, later Upbeat, a software-powered PR service
pivots.why: Founders said compelling stories were often missing from companies' outreach (VentureBeat 2017).

outcome_analysis: The YC Summer 2010 entry traces to Crowdbooster, which the founders pivoted into PRX in 2015 and renamed Upbeat. Upbeat raised a $1.5M seed in June 2017 and reached about 300 customers. A single secondary profile says it shut down about two years later because it still operated like an agency, but no first-party shutdown notice was found, so the cause is only thinly sourced.
notes: The YC page lists Upbeat in S2010 with founders David Tran and Mark Linsey, while 2017 press says the S2010 company was Crowdbooster and names Ricky Yean; the batch record likely reflects Crowdbooster, so this entry is a pivoted company and competition as of 2010 is not documented. The shutdown claim rests on a single secondary site (yespress.io), which also says the company still advertised services in 2026, unverified. The seed round is stated by VentureBeat and PYMNTS. upbeatpr.com fetch returned no content. Competition list is empty because dated sources found only name traditional PR agencies generically and nothing dated near 2010.
